steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A free press is essential for democracy: it holds power to account (investigative journalism exposed the MPs' expenses scandal), informs citizens (enabling informed voting), and provides a platform for debate. Freedom of the press is protected under Article 10 of the ECHR (freedom of expression).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Media regulation: Ofcom regulates broadcasting (TV, radio) - can impose fines and revoke licences. IPSO (Independent Press Standards Organisation) regulates newspapers - handles complaints but cannot impose fines. Some argue regulation should be stronger (Leveson Inquiry after phone-hacking scandal recommended statutory regulation of the press, but this was not fully implemented).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Media bias: all media has some bias - editorial choices about what to cover and how to frame stories. Newspaper bias: most UK national newspapers support conservative or right-wing positions (The Sun, Daily Mail, Telegraph). Broadcasters (BBC, ITV, Channel 4) are required by Ofcom to be impartial. Social media: algorithms create filter bubbles (users see content that reinforces their views).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Fake news and misinformation: deliberately false information presented as news. Spread rapidly on social media. Impact: undermines trust in institutions, distorts public debate, and can influence elections. The UK government has established the Counter Disinformation Unit; Ofcom has new duties under the Online Safety Act 2023 to protect users from harmful content.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Explain why a free press is important for democracy and evaluate whether the UK press is adequately regulated. | Q: Describe how fake news spreads and assess its impact on democratic debate. | Q: Evaluate whether social media has improved or undermined democratic participation.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Free press = essential for democracy (accountability, information, debate). Regulation = IPSO (weak) + Ofcom (stronger for broadcasting). Fake news: algorithms + confirmation bias + lack of verification. Solutions: media literacy + fact-checking + regulation. Social media: EXPANDS participation (activism, voice) but also CHEAPENS it (clicktivism, abuse, echo chambers).
